issues.t: Transmission slips, drops into neutral or shifts hard
issues.sym: Slipping or flaring revs between gears, the transmission suddenly acting like it is in neutral, harsh shifts from Park into Drive or Reverse (worse when cold), or fluid leaks.
issues.why: The Bravada uses GM's 4L60-E four-speed automatic. Automatic transmission complaints are the most common powertrain problem across these years, and GM issued a bulletin for harsh engagement on later models.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips or loses drive, avoid highway driving and have a transmission shop diagnose it before it fails completely.

issues.t: Intake manifold gaskets leak coolant
issues.sym: Coolant level dropping with no visible leak, a sweet smell, the engine running hot, a low coolant light, or misfires and rough running.
issues.why: The original intake manifold gaskets on the 4.3L Vortec V6 have a plastic core that breaks down with heat cycles, often from about 50,000 miles. Coolant can leak outside or into the engine oil.
issues.next: Don't keep topping off coolant without finding the leak. Check the oil for a milky look. Have the gaskets replaced with updated metal-core gaskets before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Spider fuel injector leaks or misfires
issues.sym: Long cranking before it starts, rough idle and stumbling at low speed that smooths out at higher rpm, a fuel smell, and misfire codes.
issues.why: The 4.3L uses a central "spider" injector assembly that can leak at its pressure regulator and lines, flooding cylinders with fuel.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure tested and the misfire codes checked. Replace the injector assembly if it is leaking; a fuel leak under the intake is also a fire risk.

issues.t: Misfire from a worn distributor cap and rotor
issues.sym: The check engine light with misfire codes (P0300 to P0306), shaking at idle, weak acceleration, or slow starts.
issues.why: The plastic distributor cap on the 4.3L sits in a hot spot and warps, wearing the rotor and its bushing.
issues.next: A new cap and rotor are often the first thing to check for misfires on this engine.

issues.t: Rough idle or stalling from the idle control valve or throttle sensor
issues.sym: Rough or surging idle, stalling at stops, hesitation, or code P0122.
issues.why: The idle air control valve clogs with deposits and the throttle position sensor wears out on the 4.3L.
issues.next: Have the throttle body cleaned and the sensors tested. Stalling in traffic is a safety risk, so don't put it off.

issues.t: AWD shudder or clunk in tight turns
issues.sym: A shudder, binding or clunk when turning sharply at low speed on dry pavement, or AWD warning lights.
issues.why: The full-time AWD transfer case can shudder. GM issued bulletins for transfer case shudder and low-speed turning vibration, and NHTSA complaints mention the transfer case.
issues.next: Make sure all four tires are the same size and evenly worn. Have the transfer case fluid changed and the unit checked.

issues.t: Cooling fan roars or engine runs hot
issues.sym: The engine fan roars constantly, or the temperature climbs in traffic. The transmission may shift late.
issues.why: The 4.2L six uses an electronically controlled fan clutch that commonly fails. On 2002 models, GM also reprogrammed the engine computer for excessive fan noise and late shifts.
issues.next: If the gauge climbs, pull over and let it cool. Have the fan clutch tested and ask about software updates.

issues.t: Cracked cylinder liner on the early 4.2L six
issues.sym: Coolant loss, white exhaust smoke, overheating or a misfire.
issues.why: Some early 4.2L engines developed cracked cylinder liners. GM extended the engine warranty to 7 years or 100,000 miles, which has ended.
issues.next: If you lose coolant with no outside leak or see white smoke, stop driving and have a cooling system and combustion leak test done.

issues.t: Ignition switch failure: gauges die and transmission sticks in third
issues.sym: The instrument panel goes dead while driving and the transmission stays in third gear.
issues.why: A failing ignition switch can cut power to the cluster and transmission controls.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have the ignition switch tested. Losing gauges while driving is unsafe, so fix it promptly.

issues.t: Blower runs only on some speeds or quits
issues.sym: The fan works on only certain settings, stops completely, or keeps running with the key off.
issues.why: The blower motor control module on this platform fails often; a revised module was released.
issues.next: Replace the blower control module. If it runs with the key off, unplug it to save the battery until fixed.

issues.t: Power window pops when going up
issues.sym: A popping noise when raising a window.
issues.why: The plastic guide on the window regulator, the same part used in the TrailBlazer, rubs the glass.
issues.next: Tape on the regulator where it touches the glass is GM's fix; the regulator usually doesn't need replacing.

issues.t: Rear sits low from a failed air suspension compressor
issues.sym: The rear end sags, especially with a load, the compressor runs a long time or not at all, or a service suspension message appears.
issues.why: Bravadas with the rear load-leveling air suspension (standard on 2WD, optional on AWD) often lose air from worn air springs or a failed compressor. RepairPal lists it as the most common Bravada problem.
issues.next: A sagging rear can upset headlight aim and handling. Have the air springs and compressor tested; some owners convert to regular coil springs.

issues.t: Fuel vapor smell from a cracked tank inlet valve
issues.sym: A gasoline smell around the rear of the truck, especially after filling up.
issues.why: The check valve where the filler pipe enters the fuel tank can crack, letting vapor and droplets escape. GM offered special coverage for this.
issues.next: Have the tank inlet checked if you smell fuel. Ask a GM dealer whether any special coverage still applies.

issues.t: AWD lights flash and AWD stops working
issues.sym: The 4WD or AWD indicator flashes and the system stops sending power to the front, with codes like C0327.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for the 4WD/AWD lamps flashing and the system becoming inoperative, often traced to the transfer case encoder or wiring.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Drive carefully on slippery roads until it is repaired.

issues.t: Rattle or clunk over bumps from stabilizer links
issues.sym: A rattle, clunk or pop from the front on rough roads.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin calling for replacement of worn stabilizer links.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected; links are a common fix but rule out ball joints too.

issues.t: Driveshaft can puncture the fuel tank in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign in normal driving.
issues.why: In some crashes the front driveshaft could contact and rupture the fuel tank, leaking fuel (recall 96V234000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Any fuel smell or drip needs inspection before driving.

issues.t: Wipers work on and off (recall)
issues.sym: The windshield wipers stop, work only sometimes, or quit in bad weather.
issues.why: Cracked solder joints in the wiper circuit and a failure-prone wiper motor led to recalls, including 03V159000.
issues.next: Don't drive in rain or snow if the wipers act up. Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Ball joints can corrode and separate (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front, wandering steering, or uneven tire wear. In the worst case the front suspension can collapse.
issues.why: Corrosion can cause the upper and lower ball joints to fail. GM recalled these trucks (01V200000).
issues.next: If the front end clunks or steering feels loose, stop driving and have the ball joints inspected. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Seat belt buckles may release in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign; a buckle may seem to latch normally.
issues.why: Some buckles could malfunction in a severe crash. GM recalled the trucks to replace them.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the buckles replaced if listed.

issues.t: Rear brake pipe can crack (recall)
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, brake fluid under the rear axle, or sudden loss of rear braking.
issues.why: The brake pipe on the rear axle could fatigue and crack. GM recalled these trucks.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. If the pedal feels soft or you see fluid, don't drive it. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Lower control arm nuts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front, the truck pulling, or a change in steering feel.
issues.why: Some lower control arm nuts on AWD trucks were not tightened enough, and the arm could separate from the frame. GM recalled them.
issues.next: Stop driving and have the front suspension checked if it clunks or pulls. Confirm the recall with your VIN.

issues.t: Brake lights and rear hazards can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights don't come on, rear hazards don't flash, or a turn signal acts up.
issues.why: The multifunction switch can develop an open circuit. GM recalled the trucks to replace the hazard switch carrier (01V364000 and 08V231000).
issues.next: Ask someone to check your brake lights. Don't drive without working brake lights; check your VIN for both recalls.

issues.t: Front lower control arm bracket can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking, wandering or pulling, or the front end sitting crooked.
issues.why: The front lower control arm brackets could fracture and separate from the frame. GM replaced them under recall 01V126000. Owners have also reported corroded rear suspension brackets.
issues.next: Stop driving if the front end clunks or pulls. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Fuel filter line can come apart (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls or won't start, a fuel smell, or fuel dripping under the truck.
issues.why: The fuel filter fitting could disconnect, causing a stall, loss of power steering assist and a fire risk. Recall 02V121000 replaced the retainers.
issues.next: If you smell fuel or see drips, don't start it. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can crack (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign.
issues.why: The driver airbag inflator could fracture at a weld when it deploys, sending fragments toward occupants. Recall 02V222000 replaced affected modules.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and get it done if open.

issues.t: Air suspension can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls or won't restart on trucks with rear air suspension.
issues.why: A power spike from the air suspension compressor can damage the engine computer. Recall 04V289000 added a wiring harness.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for the recall, especially if your Bravada has rear air suspension.

issues.t: Instrument cluster may not power up (recall)
issues.sym: Gauges and warning lights don't come on when you start the truck.
issues.why: Some clusters didn't fully power up at startup. Dealers reprogrammed them under recall 03V096000.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Don't drive without working gauges.

issues.t: Front seat belts may not lock (recall)
issues.sym: No obvious sign; the belt may not lock up in a crash.
issues.why: One of two sensors in the front belt retractors could be inoperative. Recall 04V201000 replaced faulty retractors.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Wipers stop or washer keeps running (recall)
issues.sym: Wipers won't start, stop mid-use, or the washer pump keeps running.
issues.why: Water can enter the wiper module and short it. Recall 04V046000 sealed and repaired the module.
issues.next: Don't drive in bad weather without working wipers. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Key or shifter can leave Park with the engine off (recall)
issues.sym: The key comes out with the shifter not in Park, or the shifter moves out of Park with the engine off.
issues.why: Mechanical overrides didn't meet federal theft-protection rules. Recall 03V075000 disabled them.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Brake light bulbs flicker and fail (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights or rear turn signals flicker or stop working.
issues.why: Heat and vibration can loosen the tail/stop lamp bulb in its socket. Recall 04V527000 inspected and replaced the lamp assemblies.
issues.next: Have someone check your brake lights. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Left front brake pipe can crack (recall)
issues.sym: A longer pedal travel, a soft pedal or brake fluid near the left front wheel.
issues.why: A manufacturing score on the left front brake pipe could cause it to crack. Recall 03V151000 replaced the pipe.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Don't drive if the pedal is soft or fluid is leaking. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Turn signals flash like hazards (recall)
issues.sym: Using the turn signal makes all corner lights flash like hazards.
issues.why: A faulty flasher module was replaced under recall 05V198000.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall.
